text: Shalva Papuashvili - Some European bureaucrats do not understand geography, they think that you can bypass Georgia and connect Europe to Asia - no one has ever won a struggle against geography (06.05.2026, 17:39)

"Some European bureaucrats think that you can bypass Georgia and connect Europe to Asia that way—no one has ever won a battle against geography!" — the Chairman of the Parliament, Shalva Papuashvili, stated today.
According to Papuashvili, "those bureaucrats who think they can achieve anything by bypassing Georgia and ignoring it will once again be defeated by geography."

"It has been this way for centuries—the Silk Road did not pass through here for nothing... It passed because then, just as now, it was the shortest and safest connecting route between Europe and Asia. Some bureaucrats are not well-versed in geography. As we saw in a recent report, among them, the French Minister for European Affairs could not find Iran on the map. Likewise, they often cannot find where Georgia is. Some European bureaucrats think that you can leap over Georgia and connect Europe and Asia that way—no one has ever won a struggle against geography," stated Shalva Papuashvili.

Shalva Papuashvili - In the form of the European Parliament, we have the reincarnation of the Soviet Union's Congress of People's Deputies, while we think in a European way, as a democratic country; there is a value gap between us (06.05.2026, 17:46)

In the form of the European Parliament, we have a reincarnation of the Congress of People's Deputies of the Soviet Union. There is a value gap between us. The Georgian people have nothing in common with people of Soviet mentality, Gorbachev's comrades-in-arms, and people distinguished by fascist statements - stated the Speaker of the Parliament, Shalva Papuashvili, to journalists in response to a question regarding the report on Georgia adopted by the European Parliament's Committee on Foreign Affairs.
As Papuashvili noted, the Georgian side has less and less to discuss with the European Parliament.

We see that we have less and less to talk about with these people. We are at two different poles in terms of values. In the form of the European Parliament, we have a reincarnation of the Soviet Union's Congress of People's Deputies, in the full sense of the word, in every way—the aesthetics, Rasa Juknevičienė's Russian accent, absolutely everything; it is already a complete reincarnation of the Congress of People's Deputies, while we think in a European way, we think like a democratic country, so there is a gap in values between us. We have nothing in common, and nor can we have, with that kind of value "ajapsandali" [mishmash] that is happening in the European Parliament today.

"This EU institution must change qualitatively so that the Parliament of Georgia and Georgia can have any kind of relationship with it. The Georgian people have nothing in common with people of Soviet mentality, Gorbachev's comrades, and people distinguished by fascist statements," Papuashvili stated.

Shalva Papuashvili - Zelensky has the Prime Minister of Georgia on the list of sanctioned individuals and now he had to approach and talk to him - this indicates how wrong the Ukrainian government's policy towards the Georgian people was (05.05.2026, 14:59)

"I think the initiative shown by President Zelenskyy to speak with the Prime Minister of Georgia shows that any policy that is inherently unfair is doomed to failure," stated the Chairman of the Parliament of Georgia, Shalva Papuashvili.
According to him, the President of Ukraine has Georgian Prime Minister Kobakhidze on the sanctions list, and now he had to approach him and have a conversation.

„I think this speaks for itself regarding how erroneous the Ukrainian government's policy toward the Georgian people was, and it gives me hope that this is a sign of rethinking—that acting against the Georgian people yields no results, and betting on forces fed by the betrayal of the Georgian people will not bring good results. Once again, we have always said—not only regarding Ukraine, but regarding all those countries and governments engaged in various kinds of unfair policies toward the population of Georgia—that we remain in a format of one-sided friendship, which implies that we are in the right in these relations. Whoever took a wrong step regarding Georgia will, in the end, hopefully realize the error of their own actions. We are always ready to rethink all these relations.“

For more than 4 years, unfortunately, we have seen a policy from the Ukrainian government that is not only directed against the Georgian people but also does not serve the interests of the Ukrainian people. For 4 years, we have seen that this relationship has reached the point where it is precisely due to the decisions of the Ukrainian government. In this relationship, we have always emphasized that Georgia and the Georgian government have always supported the Ukrainian people and Ukraine; there is no resolution that we have not supported. If anyone needs to take a step and make amends, it is the Ukrainian government.

"When you impose sanctions on government representatives who stand by your country and people, it is anything but an expression of gratitude. As for other behaviors, we have all witnessed this; we saw it with our own eyes and heard it with our own ears when President Zelensky directly demanded that the Georgian government organize fighters and send them to Ukraine to fight, and thereby openly become involved as a party in the Russia-Ukraine war. In Georgian, this is called 'being dragged into war'; I don't know what they call it in Ukrainian," stated Papuashvili.

Shalva Papuashvili - It is symbolic that a few days before May 9, Juknevičienė, who is distinguished by fascist statements, is the author of the resolution - the European Parliament is presenting itself as the successor to the Congress of People's Deputies of the Soviet Union (05.05.2026, 14:52)

"In a few days, we will have another commemoration of the Day of Victory over Fascism, and it is symbolic that a few days before May 9, Juknevičienė, who is distinguished by her fascist statements towards the Georgian people, is the author of this resolution," stated the Chairman of the Parliament of Georgia, Shalva Papuashvili.

As Papuashvili noted in response to a question regarding the report on Georgia adopted by the European Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee, the European Parliament confirms once again that day by day it is establishing itself as the "successor to the Congress of People's Deputies of the Soviet Union."

As for the next hostile report or resolution being prepared against the Georgian people, there is nothing new in this. Once again, the European Parliament confirms that day by day it is establishing itself as the successor to the Congress of People's Deputies of the Soviet Union. It presents itself as the successor to the People's Congress of the Soviet Union. This is not surprising, considering that we see Soviet citizens in the ranks of the European Parliament—representatives of the Soviet nomenclature or elite who are ensconced in the European Parliament. I am referring to the representatives of the Baltic states and some Eastern European countries. Just as the Moscow Union Congress used to make hostile decisions regarding Georgia, so too does the Brussels Union Parliament make such hostile decisions today.

"The author of the report for this resolution is Juknevičienė, who is distinguished by fascist statements towards the Georgian people, which is noteworthy. In a few days, we will have another celebration of Victory Day over Fascism, and it is symbolic that a few days before May 9, the person, Juknevičienė, who is distinguished by fascist statements towards the Georgian people, is the author of this resolution," notes Papuashvili.
Furthermore, according to Papuashvili, "it is precisely Brussels and foreign funding that are killing free media in Georgia and subjugating the media for their own propaganda."

Regarding the question related to the revision of visa-free travel, whether "Georgian Dream" feels responsibility for it. According to the Speaker of the Parliament, "Mikheil Saakashvili's fan club will threaten the Georgian people with various instruments."
"As for the European Parliament, Mikheil Saakashvili's fan club should not lecture us on any values, any rules, or any law; they are Mikheil Saakashvili's fan club, and that says it all."
When you are a member of the fan club of a dictator, a torturer, a corrupt person, it is a verdict.

It is clear that Mikheil Saakashvili's fan club will threaten the Georgian people with various instruments. There is nothing surprising in this. Just as they have tried to harm us at other times, ultimately, they will not achieve this. They will not achieve the main thing: for the Georgian people to act according to their political agenda.

"They are interested neither in Georgian journalism nor in the well-being of the Georgian people; the only thing that Juknevičienė and people with similar obsessive ideas are interested in is using Georgia as a weapon against Russia. We are seen as a weapon against Russia; they see no other purpose for our people," stated Shalva Papuashvili.
Shalva Papuashvili - Today's disrupted international system is characterized by geopolitical tension, economic uncertainty, and shifting security dynamics. (07.05.2026, 13:57)

"It is a great honor for me to participate in the discussion on parliamentary diplomacy within the framework of the first summit of Speakers and Presidents of Parliaments of PAM member and partner countries. Georgia's historical ties with the Mediterranean region date back millennia, and we are pleased to continue this tradition since officially gaining independence 35 years ago," - stated the Chairman of the Parliament of Georgia, Shalva Papuashvili, during his speech at the first summit of Speakers of Parliaments of the member and partner countries of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Mediterranean (PAM).
As Shalva Papuashvili noted, today's disrupted international system is characterized by geopolitical tensions, economic uncertainty, and changing security dynamics.

According to him, society is witnessing the collapse of the rules-based international order, which is an alarming process and calls into question the foundations of stability, cooperation, and trust between states.

"It is a special honor to address you from the position of the President of PABSEC, which gives me the opportunity to voice the concerns of the parliamentarians of the Black Sea region countries. Today, our region is at the epicenter of global instability – the Russia-Ukraine war is ongoing, which has already lasted for more than four years."

How can parliamentary diplomacy promote regional peace and inter-regional cooperation? At a time when global organizations fail to achieve results, regional formats are given a unique opportunity to change reality for the better: we are united by common pragmatic interests, which are directly delegated to us by our population, as parliaments directly express the will of the people.

Accordingly, regional unions create a framework through which neighboring countries can conduct dialogue, discuss common challenges, and reach practical solutions. The Mediterranean, Black Sea, and Gulf regions are interconnected spaces where enhanced cooperation can bring tangible results. Enhanced parliamentary exchanges may become a bridge for stability, innovation, and sustainable development. These connections will provide additional chances for peace.
Which main directions of interregional cooperation can we highlight to achieve peace and stability?

"Connectivity occupies a central place in this cooperation. The development of strategic transit routes, including the Middle Corridor, is reshaping trade and economic relations between Europe and Asia. These corridors are channels of cooperation that bring our regions closer together and reduce the vulnerability of global supply chains. The issue of connectivity is closely linked to energy security, which has become a decisive theme for our common future. The diversification of energy sources and routes is essential for ensuring stability and resilience, especially for Europe. By strengthening cooperation on alternative energy resources and infrastructure, we will promote economic growth and create a more secure and sustainable energy environment," stated Shalva Papuashvili.
Shalva Papuashvili addresses Pawel Herczynski with a letter (08.05.2026, 10:34)
The Speaker of the Parliament of Georgia, Shalva Papuashvili, addresses the EU Ambassador, Pawel Herczynski, with a letter.
Papuashvili publishes a letter on social media and writes that he is addressing Herczynski regarding Europe Day.

„Happy Europe Day. On this important day, beyond the symbolic celebration, we must reflect on what Europe actually is, how its significance is reflected in the lives of citizens, and how it shapes the future of Georgia and the European Union.“

Robert Schuman, one of the founding fathers of the European Union and a great French statesman, made his historic statement on this very day, the fifth anniversary of the end of the Second World War. The "Schuman Declaration" was based on one primary goal: to ensure that war would never again devastate Europe. The spirit of the declaration was clear – peace through unity, cooperation through mutual respect, and stability through shared responsibility. The European Union's current policies should be evaluated precisely against the backdrop of this vision.

Unlike Robert Schuman, last year, on Europe Day, in your address to the Georgian people, you chose to ignore the anniversary of the end of the Second World War and, instead, focused on your political grievances against the host country. However, it is perhaps worth reminding that without the parents and grandparents of today's generations of the Georgian people, alongside other anti-fascist nations, fascism would not have been defeated, and neither the European Union nor Europe Day would exist. In Georgia, there is no family that did not make a sacrifice in this war. The separation of Europe Day from Victory Day is unacceptable to us. Therefore, I hope that on May 9, at your gathering, you will pay proper tribute to the 300,000 Georgians who laid down their lives for a Europe free from fascism.

"European unity was not achieved and we got war" - the actions of the current leadership of the European Union show that it fails to comprehend this fundamental conclusion of the Schuman Declaration. The current policy of the European Union leaves no room for any other explanation than that it is aimed at deepening confrontation and increasing disagreements. The unfair and politically motivated resolutions of the European Parliament, numerous threats of political and economic revenge, constant interference in Georgia's internal affairs - these are just a few examples of the deliberate attempts aimed at inciting confrontation both within Georgia and in Georgia-EU relations. A truly united Europe is one that not only prevents future wars but also ends current conflicts. However, unfortunately, in Brussels' policy towards Georgia, the intention to achieve unity between the Georgian people and the European Union is nowhere to be seen.

"Europe will not be made all at once, or according to a single plan," stated Robert Schuman in his famous declaration. Unfortunately, today we see that these wise words of Schuman are ignored, while the European Union's policy is implemented based on narrow political interests and false and artificially created ideologies that disregard the cultural richness, ideological diversity, and political pluralism of the European population. The attempt to impose political and ideological frameworks on Georgia on its path to European integration is a good example of this narrow, futile, and superficial policy.

The Georgian people do not need to be shown the direction toward the European path. Georgia itself is a co-creator of European civilization, and therefore, wherever Georgia is, there is Europe as well. European integration should not mean Brussels' unilateral dominance over Georgia, but rather it should be the true strengthening of our historical ties with other European nations, as equals.

Europe Day should also remind us that no leadership of the European Union can abolish such European ideals as national independence, Christian values, and the traditional way of life, simply because they hold different ideological views. It is precisely an incompatibility with this founding spirit of the European Union that is revealed by those who are overly preoccupied with so-called "regime change" plans against democratically elected governments, impose ideologies incompatible with human nature, and, by ignoring existing differences in traditions, attempt to establish a uniform way of life.

The idea of creating the "Coal and Steel Community," presented by Robert Schuman on May 9, 1950, aimed at "raising the standard of living and maintaining achievements." He understood well that peace requires a solid economic foundation. The entire European project was based on this very idea. However, today the EU leadership seems to have forgotten even this basic principle. How else can one explain the persistent calls to engage in economic confrontation against Russia without offering any security guarantees or economic support—calls which, if followed, would lead not only to Georgia's economic collapse but also to regional instability, leaving Europe without significant energy resources and geoeconomic routes.

The deviation from the initial European aspirations embedded in the idea of Europe Day has led the European Union to a state where its policy towards Georgia is reduced to the support of violence, hate speech, and radicalism. Last year, twice, I addressed you in writing with a call to condemn the frequent instances of hate speech and violence, though to no avail. The severe consequences of the politically motivated turning a blind eye to violence and radicalism were most clearly seen on October 4 of last year, when the lighting of a rhetorical green light for violence by the well-known statement of the EU spokesperson led radical groups to storm the Presidential Palace. Since then, for more than seven months now, not a single high-ranking European official has publicly condemned this coup attempt, as if violent coups were a normal practice in European politics.

The latest unacceptable and threatening statements made regarding Georgia towards our people, as if the country is returning to a "dark past," once again demonstrate how wrong the European Union's current policy is. However, if we look at the reality from the perspective of the Georgian people, it may be Europe itself that is heading toward that dark past which Robert Schuman and other great figures of his generation tried to avoid.

Georgia has a clear offer for the path forward. Ending aggressive rhetoric, revising harmful policies, and repealing unjust resolutions is what would open the way for genuine dialogue, reasonableness, and unity, which is indeed the original spirit of Europe Day.

"If we want Europe Day to maintain its significance, then it must once again mean what it originally represented – peace, cooperation, and unity, based on respect for nations and their identity," reads Papuashvili's letter.
